node.title: Re: Date to Epoch (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
perl -MPOSIX -e 'print strptime(, "%s")'

For some reason, Perl's [doc://POSIX] does not provide strptime, you'd need to install and use [mod://POSIX::strptime].

But if you have or can install the module [doc://Time::Piece] (in core since 5.10), you can use its Time::Piece->strptime(STRING, FORMAT), it has a nicer interface.

Update:

$ echo "Mar 20 2018 09:00" | perl -wMstrict -MTime::Piece -nle 'print Time::Piece->strptime($_,"%b %d %Y %H:%M")->epoch' 1521536400

If you want to use POSIX::strptime, you should also look into [man://mktime], although at that point I'd really recommend using a better module. I usually use [mod://DateTime] because it supports almost everything you'd need, but for simple tasks [doc://Time::Piece] is enough.
